concept.centerRule: Only explicit Eden, Paradise, tree-of-life, expulsion, covenant-land loss, historical exile/return, or tightly evidenced Scripture reuse carries the Concept. Similar imagery alone does not establish identity.

characterAnchors.label: Adam and Eve
characterAnchors.note: Receive garden life, cross its command, and are sent beyond its guarded boundary.

characterAnchors.label: Cain
characterAnchors.note: Becomes a marked wanderer and settles east of Eden after Abel’s blood cries from the ground.

characterAnchors.label: Abraham
characterAnchors.note: Leaves country, lives as a stranger, and receives land and return promises for descendants.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: Carries land promise, covenant warning, wilderness memory, scattering, and return before Israel.

characterAnchors.label: Israel and Judah
characterAnchors.note: Receive land, lose kingdoms and sanctuary, live among nations, and become the subjects of gathering promises.

characterAnchors.label: Jerusalem / Zion
characterAnchors.note: Appears as city, bereaved woman, remembered home, restored gathering place, and final-city memory.

characterAnchors.label: Ezekiel
characterAnchors.note: Sees departing and returning glory, restored land, river, trees, city, and Eden imagery applied to rulers.

characterAnchors.label: The returned remnant
characterAnchors.note: Rebuilds worship and city life while confession preserves continuing servitude and incompleteness.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus Christ
characterAnchors.note: Is tested in wilderness, promises Paradise, opens living-water and dwelling language, and anchors Adam’s later contrast.

characterAnchors.label: John
characterAnchors.note: Receives visions of Paradise, new creation, open city, river, tree, face, and ended curse.

concept.throughline: Eden begins as gifted place and guarded life; later land, sanctuary, exile, return, Paradise, Adam, and new-creation sources repeatedly reopen questions of presence, access, home, and restored life.
